The 20 carried-over trigger cases hold their last measured verdicts (2026-07-28 revalidation for issue #294: recall 10/10, specificity 10/10) as a baseline only; the 4 added cases have never been measured, and the description they measure changed in this rewrite. _meta.run_from: dist/housecarl/skills/open-animation-replacer/ - the PACKAGED tree, not .claude/skills/. The packager strips evals/, so the suite is driven from outside the tree it tests, which is also the check that no body pointer dangles in dist/.

arms.trigger: Which ONE skill a fresh-context agent loads for a query, measured with-skill and without-skill.
arms.output_quality: The audit's own DAR-to-OAR task on the live order, run as a pair: control (no housecarl:* skill in the catalogue) against with-skill. Eval id 25.

method.cases: 24 trigger cases - 12 should-trigger, 12 should-not - plus 1 output-quality case. The 24 trigger cases are the ones carrying should_trigger; eval 25 carries arm='output_quality' and no should_trigger, so a runner splitting on should_trigger never scores it as a which-skill pick and recall is computed over 12. The shipped 20 (10/10) survive with their queries unchanged; 4 are added for the description's changed clauses (2 positives naming the front-loaded terms, 2 near-miss negatives for the new exclusion clause).
method.split: 60/40 train/held-out; best iteration chosen by held-out score; at most 5 iterations.
method.without_skill_arm: MANDATORY (rewrite ruling 3). Every query runs twice, with and without this skill in the catalogue, each run from a clean context in a separate session or subagent - never the authoring session. Results are reported as a delta, not as an absolute rate. The without-skill arm is also how a negative case is shown to be a near-miss rather than an unreachable prompt.
method.coexistence: A neutral menu of realistic sibling skills, this skill not flagged as under test.
method.isolation: This skill alone in the menu, plus NONE. Each of the five gate dimensions - triggering accuracy, isolation, coexistence, instruction following, output quality - carries a named failure mode recorded per run.
method.models: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus, results recorded per tier. No Fable-model agents.
method.grading: Each expectation is PASS or FAIL with evidence that quotes the output. No partial credit, and no prediction-scored headline.
method.cost: total_tokens and duration_ms recorded per run, next to the pass-rate delta, and reported against the audit's own 23-call / 4-reference-call baseline.
method.release_gate: The full suite runs before promoting a version, and specifically on any houseCARL tool-surface change. The surface change that killed the two 1.x tool names in SKILL.md triggered no re-run, which is how they reached dist/.

last_measured.run: 2026-07-28 revalidation (issue #294), against the PRE-rewrite description and the 20-case set

evals.prompt: Convert the DAR folder .../animations/DynamicAnimationReplacer/_CustomConditions/2000030002/ to a native OAR submod config.json, and answer whether any OAR submod in the load order wins over it for the animations it replaces.
evals.expected_output: A single config.json whose priority is 2000030002 and whose conditions are the converted chain, plus an answer to the who-wins half that compares priorities across native OAR and legacy DAR submods. The audit's own two candidate configs are the reference answer; the control's output is diffed against them.
evals.input_files_note: The four inputs live beside the audit log at dev/skill-validation/audit-2026-09/oar-authoring/with-skill/ (_conditions.txt, _WoodcutterAxe.txt, config.json, config.intended.json). They are not copied into the shipped tree: dev/ is untracked, and the packager strips evals/ anyway.
expectations: The run states that OAR sorts every targeting submod by priority descending and that plugin/ESP load order is ignored, and does not inspect MO2 mod order to answer who wins.
The run treats 2000030002 - the DAR folder's own name - as a priority in the same global space as native OAR integers, and compares it against them.

Every child array inside AND/OR/XOR in the emitted config.json is capital-C Conditions and the submod's top-level array is lowercase conditions. Graded by parsing the emitted file, not by reading the prose: a file that parses cleanly with the wrong casing is a FAIL.

The AND/OR binding is applied as the settled rule, not raised as an open question: OR binds tighter than AND, so each run of OR-terminated lines becomes one OR condition and the groups are AND-ed with the remaining terms. A run that emits a flat left-to-right chain FAILS, and so does one that presents the binding as ambiguous and picks a reading.
The competing-submod scan is enumerated with housecarl_asset_status and an under= glob rather than a raw filesystem walk, and the answer names the VFS winner per config.
evals.conditions: ARR 2.0 order (3,801 plugins), 40-call cap, fresh context, no other housecarl:* skill in the catalogue. Identical task in both arms.
evals.pass_rule: Beating the control = the with-skill arm passes all five and the control fails at least one of the first four. If the control passes all five, that is reported to Aaron as evidence about whether this skill earns its catalogue entry, not explained away.
